newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean union postpones strikes set for Feb 18.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean union postpones strikes set for Feb 18.

text.p: South Korea's outlawed labour union said on Thursday it decided to postpone strikes until after it sees how parliament handles the revision of a controversial new labour law.
The Korean Confederation of Trade Unions said the strikes would now start between February 24-28. They had originally been scheduled to begin on February 18.

The confederation said in a statement it could go on strike before February 24 if the revised draft of the law did not meet the standards of international labour law or eroded the living standards of Korean workers.
Parliament has agreed to reopen on February 17 for a 30-day session to discuss possible revision of the labour law and the scandal over failed Hanbo Steel Co.
The steel flagship of the Hanbo Group racked up five trillion won ($5.8 billion) in loans before being declared insolvent on January 23.

South Korea was hit by almost a month of labour strife from late December after the ruling party rammed a new labour law through parliament making it easier for companies to sack workers and replace strikers.
